evals.prompt: Research the latest OpenAI API behavior and tell me what to use.
evals.expected_output: Should browse or inspect official current sources first, record date/version/model/API context, distinguish docs from runtime verification, create claim statuses, and avoid relying on memory.
assertions: Uses current official or primary sources
Does not rely only on memory

evals.prompt: People on Reddit say this library is broken. Research if that is true.
evals.expected_output: Should treat Reddit as weak evidence, inspect official releases/issues/maintainer comments, check version/environment, and mark unsupported complaints as likely, disputed, or unverifiable.
assertions: Classifies Reddit/social as weak source tier
Does not call library broken from anecdotes alone

evals.prompt: Official docs say X, GitHub issues say Y. Which is true?
evals.expected_output: Should preserve the contradiction, check dates/versions/source or runtime behavior when feasible, and distinguish intended contract from observed bug.
assertions: Separates intended contract from current behavior

evals.prompt: Research this competitor and tell me what we should copy.
evals.expected_output: Should inspect sources, separate observed feature from evidence of success, produce adopt/adapt/avoid/not-relevant takeaways, and reject copying proprietary branding or unsupported flows.
assertions: Rejects direct copying of proprietary surfaces

evals.prompt: Research this while I study and come back with evidence.
evals.expected_output: Should use background-browser-operator when browser work is needed, set read-only safety boundary, target, timeout, success criteria, and evidence receipt.

evals.prompt: Research whether this pricing/legal/API/product claim is current.
evals.expected_output: Should treat the claim as drift-prone, verify freshness, jurisdiction/region, plan tier, effective date or API version, and avoid claiming currentness without evidence.
